blanks.section: Why tests are used and debated

blanks.sentence: Assessing possible harm involves the _____ of thousands of experimental results.

multipleChoice.question: How do the two sides of the animal-testing debate differ?
options: Supporters stress human safety; campaigners question both welfare and effectiveness.
Both accept the tests as accurate but disagree about their cost.
Supporters seek fewer medicines; campaigners seek more safety checks.
Both question animal welfare but disagree about which species to use.

multipleChoice.question: What has led groups on both sides of the debate to reconsider animal testing?
options: A change in the number of legally required animal types.
New evidence that medicines affect all species alike.
The possible contribution of artificial intelligence.
A decision to begin tests with human volunteers.

multipleChoice.question: What does the example of substances toxic to animals but safe for humans suggest?
options: Animal tests can help identify every risk to humans.
A substance safe for one species is usually safe for another.
Substances harmful to animals should first be tested on people.
Animal results do not always predict human results reliably.

multipleChoice.question: Why is AI potentially useful when assessing whether a new medicine may harm people?
options: It can remove the need to examine experimental results.
It is good at analysing very large amounts of data.
It can ensure all experimental results agree.
It can rule out the need to assess newly invented chemicals.

multipleChoice.question: Why may the work of assessing chemical safety keep growing?
options: New chemicals continue to be created alongside the existing data burden.
Existing data become unusable whenever a chemical is invented.
Scientists must repeat all previous tests for every new medicine.
AI generates more chemicals than scientists can evaluate.

multipleChoice.question: Which conclusion best reflects the discussion's view of AI and future animal testing?
options: AI has already made testing on animals unnecessary.
AI may help reduce or eventually end such testing, but it is only part of the solution.
AI offers no benefit until it can replace every safety check.
AI will certainly end animal testing within a few years.
